parsedVerdict.reasoning: ReceivingService is a business-layer service. It coordinates domain use cases: receive puts stock into a bin, and pick takes stock from several bins and works out whether to reorder. The stock rules stay in the domain objects (Bin.put, Bin.take, Item.needsReorder). Unknown items and bins raise a domain error (StockError). The service never touches storage directly: it has no SQL, connection or transaction handling, and no transport or framework code. It only calls methods on the injected tables (find, holding, store). The private item() and bin() helpers turn stored records into Bin and Item objects, and store({ ...bin }) passes plain copies back. That is light data-mapping glue you would normally find in an application service, not real persistence logic. Depending on the concrete persistence classes (BinTable, ItemTable) is an import-direction question, which other tools check, so it is out of scope here. Every responsibility in the file fits the domain layer.
